title: Celestis POC weekly — units vs latency tradeoffs
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on tokens/sec/$ and perceived latency impact from caching and batching. Customer validated that prefix caching yields largest unit savings for their prompt shapes; batching helps with throughput but increases tail latency for short queries. SE proposed config changes and next benchmark runs. Action items assigned for two follow-up experiments and a pricing/practicality email to the procurement team.
topics: next benchmark runs and procurement ask
action_items: Priya: share 48-hour sample of real request lengths (CSV) by 2026-08-28
Sofia: run two benchmark runs (run+no-cache + run+prefix-cache+micro-batching) and upload results to sheets by 2026-08-27
Jordan: email pilot pricing delta for Dedicated vs Hosted with observed unit econ by 2026-08-26
Ethan: provide cluster logs for latency spikes (2026-08-25 to 2026-08-24) — due 2026-08-29
next_steps: Sofia to run caching + batching matrix and share sheet link
Customer to decide whether to enable prefix caching in production pilot next week
Jordan to send updated pricing and suggested Dedicated configuration
transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-08-25 14:00 PDT; Duration: 46 minutes; Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Sofia (Redwood SE), Marcus (CSM), Priya (Celestis Head ML), Ethan (Infra), Liam (PM), Nina (SRE)

Summary block (auto): weekly POC check-in, focus on tokens/sec per dollar, caching wins, and latency tradeoffs

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, uh quick roll call — I think we got the same lineup as last week, Priya, Ethan?
[00:09] Priya: yep here, sorry running a touch late, got the sample data pulled though and we'll share it in a sec
[00:16] Sofia: hi all, i'll kick off with the bench results we ran yesterday, two configs: baseline hosted small-batch and hosted with prefix/KV cache + micro-batching
[00:25] Sofia: baseline produced about 95k tokens per dollar on average for your long multi-turn flows, with tokens/sec/$ metric around 12 tokens per second per dollar equivalent, which is kind of — it's baseline numbers
[00:39] Sofia: with prefix caching enabled we saw effective tokens per dollar jump to ~340k for those conversational sessions where the prompt prefixes repeat, so roughly 3.5x savings, caveat is this is workload dependent
[00:52] Ethan: wait that 340k number, that's with KV cache warmed for each user, right? how many unique conversations did you simulate?
[01:01] Sofia: good call — we warmed cache across 10k simulated user sessions, we had the same prefix repeated across about 60% of requests which is similar to your sample patterns from last week, if your real traffic has lower prefix repeat the uplift will be smaller
[01:15] Priya: our sample shows about 45% repeat at the 5-turn window and 70% at 3-turn window — we can send the CSV, it's slightly different between product search and support flows
[01:26] Jordan: perfect, that's exactly what we need to map to expected savings; two quick notes on cost: caching reduces token rendering cost but adds memory/KV footprint on the instance, which nudges your Dedicated config -- if you go Dedicated you'll want the bigger instance type to hold caches, otherwise hosted works but cost math shifts
[01:44] Liam: can you quantify memory impact? like how big a bump per 10k users?
[01:50] Sofia: approximate numbers — 10k keys with 1.2KB average KV entry is roughly 12MB, but per-shard overhead and indexing makes it closer to 50-80MB per shard; with 8 shards you double-ish that, so plan for a few GB if you want high cache hit rates and low eviction 
[02:12] Nina: and eviction behavior — we saw a couple of tail latency spikes when eviction kicked in last run, is that a smoothing setting?
[02:19] Sofia: yep eviction can trigger backend reads which add ~30-120ms in tails if cache miss cascades; micro-batching can sometimes mask that for throughput but it also increases median for short queries
[02:31] Jordan: that leads into batching tradeoffs — for your support flow with lots of short one-off queries, micro-batching at 50ms window reduces tokens/sec/$ slightly but adds 40-90ms median, whereas for longer generation sessions it dramatically improves tokens/sec/$
[02:45] Priya: our SLOs on customer-facing support chat are 300ms p95, so we can't push batch windows too far
[02:52] Sofia: understood — we tested three windows: 0ms (no batching), 20ms micro, 80ms macro. At 20ms we saw a 22% throughput improvement and median latency +45ms; at 80ms throughput +65% but median +160ms p50, which pushes you above p95 targets
[03:12] Ethan: curious about quantization — you mentioned a 4-bit variant in the doc, what was the quality delta?
[03:18] Sofia: 4-bit QAT style had minor behavioral drifts on rare prompts, overall Rouge-like metrics were within 1.5% of FP16, token generation cost dropped another ~18% compared to the 8-bit route; we recommend sanity evals on your high-value prompts
[03:33] Priya: so if we combine prefix caching, 8-bit quant, and 20ms micro-batching, what's the rough unit econ?
[03:40] Sofia: ballpark for your mix: tokens per dollar moves from 95k up to ~260k; tokens/sec/$ also increases about 2.8x, median latency goes from ~180ms to ~235ms in that config — still within your 300ms p95 in most cases but tail behavior needs monitoring
[03:56] Priya: got it. Can you put those numbers in the sheet with the configs so Product can see tradeoffs?
[04:02] Jordan: yes — Sofia will upload the matrix; we'll include run IDs and raw logs link.
[04:07] Sofia: link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/benchmarks_celestis (note: placeholder link in transcript) — sheet has runs: run-27 baseline, run-28 prefix-cache, run-29 prefix+20ms, run-30 prefix+80ms, run-31 4bit quant+prefix
[04:23] Liam: i want to call out cost predictability — even if tokens per dollar improves, our finance team cares about variance and spikes; how do we model the worst-case?
[04:32] Marcus (CSM): we usually provide a forecast sheet with median and 95th percentiles and a recommended safety buffer; for pilots we suggest a 15-25% buffer for eviction-induced spikes
[04:41] Priya: procurement will likely ask for Dedicated numbers as that makes forecasting easier for us, but we need the delta. Jordan— can you send a Dedicated vs Hosted delta with the observed runs?
[04:51] Jordan: yes i'll send a short pricing note; initial estimate: Dedicated reduces per-token price by 12-25% depending on committed capacity and your KV footprint pushes the optimal size — we'll include three sizing options
[05:02] Ethan: technical Q on graceful degradation — if dedicated pool is saturated, will Redwood fallback to smaller quantized model or to hosted fallback? we want to avoid request errors
[05:11] Sofia: two-layer fallback we recommend: first fallback to same model with slightly higher quantization (e.g., 8-bit instead of 4-bit), second fallback route to hosted compatible variant with soft-rate limiting; in the control plane you can pick behavior per route
[05:24] Nina: can we get traces for the eviction spikes you mentioned? we'd like to correlate with our infra metrics
[05:29] Sofia: yes, run-28 and run-30 have trace IDs in the sheet, we'll share a zipped trace + flame graphs; expect some noise but should help root cause
[05:39] Priya: timeline question: if we accept prefix caching and micro-batching at 20ms, how soon can we flip it in the pilot?
[05:46] Jordan: assuming we get your final sample data and grant access for two test users, we can enable caching for the pilot cohort within 48 hours; Sofia will do a quick smoke test and we recommend a canary rollout to 5% then 25%
[05:58] Priya: good, product wants a rollout plan in writing — include the canary percentages, rollback steps, and monitoring thresholds
[06:06] Jordan: will do — action item for Jordan to draft rollout + thresholds and share with Priya and Nina this week
[06:13] Liam: any security or compliance blockers to using prefix/KV caching? our legal team asked about PII in cache keys
[06:20] Sofia: digest: Redwood supports encrypted caches and KMS integration; we recommend hashing keys and enabling TTLs and audit logs — we'll attach security notes. No elevation needed for pilot but for production we usually sign an addendum around caching PII practices
[06:34] Priya: perfect. Last thing — can you produce a short note that maps our typical session mix (support vs search) to expected monthly spend under the three configs? product and finance will need that
[06:44] Jordan: yes, Sofia will populate the modeling tab in the sheet with three scenarios: conservative, expected, optimistic; we'll include assumed prefix repeat rates per flow
[06:53] Marcus: i'll coordinate calendar for next sync; suggest same time next week unless you want more frequent for the next two runs
[07:00] Priya: weekly is fine for now. thanks for the clarity.
[07:05] Jordan: awesome thanks all — recap of action items now

Auto Action items (verbatim): Priya to share CSV sample; Sofia to run caching+batching matrix and upload; Jordan to send pricing note and rollout doc; Ethan to provide cluster logs and Nina to confirm monitoring thresholds
